question.knowledge_point: Solving a System Containing Fractions in One Equation Using Elimination
question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}-3p+\frac{4}{5}q=-1 \\ 9p-4q=-13\end{aligned}
$$

Find the solution to the system of equations given above.
question.worked_solution:
To get rid of the fractions in the first equation, we must multiply the first equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $5.$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-3p+\frac{4}{5}q=-1 & |\,\times 5 \\ 9p-4q=-13\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}-15p+4q=-5 \\ 9p-4q=-13\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that the $4q$ term in the first equation can cancel with the $-4q$ term in the second equation.

Adding the two equations eliminates the $q$-variable, and allows us to solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-15p+\cancel{4q} & =-5 \\ 9p-\cancel{4q} & =-13 \\ -6p & =-18 \\ p & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $p=3$ into the equation $9p-4q=-13$ to solve for $q:$

$$
\begin{aligned}9p-4q & =-13 \\ 9\cdot 3-4q & =-13 \\ 27-4q & =-13 \\ -4q & =-40 \\ q & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $p=3,\,q=10.$
